messages.subject: mqmplot.circle
parts:
I've been using the mqmplot.circle function for R/QTL

mqmplot.circle(multifilled6,multires6,highlight=15,transparency=T)

I am wondering if there is an issue with the "transparency="?  (I'm assuming this is the appropriate setting to stop the legends from covering up the chromosomes.)
The legends are plotted over top of the chromosomes regardless of transparency=T or F. 

Should I be using a different argument?

Also, this is on a windows 7 machine with 64-bit R.

Thanks

messages.author: 92292fc48bf46044
messages.subject: Re: mqmplot.circle
parts:
Dear jay,

Thanks for the bug report.
The transparancy option just changes the transparancy for the colors, this is needed for some journals.

Attached is an updated file (might take a while for it to come into the new version of R/qtl) for the circle plot
I made the legends slightly smaller, and put in another option to suppress the legends besides the circle plot (axis.legend=FALSE).

You can just copy past this into R (after loading the qtl package)
Hope this helps,

Danny Arends

messages.author: 92292fc48bf46044
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] mqmplot.circle
parts:
Dear Chandra,

To change the colors, you need to update the drawcirculargenome function

change on line 238:

points(locationtocircle(result,result[x,1],result[x,2],spacing=spacing),pch=20,cex=min(c((result[x,3]),4)))

to

points(locationtocircle(result,result[x,1],result[x,2],spacing=spacing),pch=20,cex=min(c((result[x,3]),4)),col="blue")

this will change the color of the circles used to draw the circular genome (blue in this case)

Gr,
Danny
